# The useful system began with a refusal

The first useful decision was a refusal. A tempting shortcut would have hidden the source of the work, so the shortcut stayed on the shelf.

The replacement was plain: one structured prompt, one visible proof, and one review before anything moved forward. The smaller system exposed its own mistakes. That made it easier to trust.

Tools are most useful when they clarify a decision. When they blur one, speed is theatre.
